answer: I'd like to know why the meeting was moved?
I'm not sure which gate our flight leaves from?
I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off?
I wonder how Anna's job interview went?
Tell your manager whether you can work on Saturday.
If your bag doesn't arrive, call the airline.

wrong_options_that_fit: 'Whether or not' is grammatical but changes the meaning to 'regardless', which is illogical here; arguable.
sense_problem: Whether or not is not clearly wrong; a strong reader may accept it (call regardless of the driver ringing makes little sense, but is not a grammar error).

answer: Everything now depends on if the bank approves our loan.
sense_problem: 'depends on if' is common in informal English, so a learner may see it as correct; only formal usage requires 'whether'.

wrong_options_that_fit: unless: 'unless we're late' is grammatical but illogical (keeping the room only if on time contradicts the point)
instruction_problem: No instruction sentence (e.g. 'Complete with the cards'); only the cards say what to do.
sense_problem: Second gap with 'whether' ('whether we're late, they'll keep...') is incomplete without 'or not', so not accepted.
